chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: His first record: the vocal with Luis Russell and microphone fright
summary: John Nesbitt took him to the session; he was uncredited and nervous, has always feared microphones but likes a megaphone.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh yeah, the way you came to make your first recording, which was the vocal with Luis Russell's band...
Yes.
Dickenson - 147
You said that John Nesbitt took you to the session.

Yeah. Well, you know, it was a (?) thing, when they... I guess when I contracted to play that number. But already, they didn't give me credit for singing. Which I wasn't a very good singer, I'll tell you that.
I've heard it!
Heh-heh, it's pretty bad. I was nervous as a... I was nervous as a what-do-you-call it...? -- I don't know.
Were you familiar with the song, or did you just...?
I had been singing the song all the time. But I always have had mike fright. I always have had it. I'm frightened of mikes. I just can't used to a mike.
Even now?
Even today I can't get used to the mikes. I don't like them.
Did you ever use a megaphone?
Yeah, I like that. I can sing with them. No trouble.
That's a more natural thing.
Yes. I guess I'm old-fashioned, that's all, as far as that's concerned.
Well, no, maybe not. Because with a microphone, you never know exactly, until you've tried the mike, how it's
Dickenson - 148
A little. You're kind of uptight, you know. Anybody gets uptight, because they don't want to make a mistake.
Even today, with tape and everything?
No one wants to make a mistake. And when you make it on records, it's there forever. You can't call back them notes.
But now, with tape and everything, they're usually able to fix things and do them over more easily than it used to be.
